text:
sam: quick thread — ran multi-model co-residency test on staging (2x 13B + 1x 7B) and saw a nasty perf/regression when kernel selection + batching heuristics hit under allocator pressure. logs attached in-line. :frowning:

lina: curious — was this on the new pooled allocator or the default cudaMalloc path?

sam: pooled allocator (the one we shipped last month). peak mem per-GPU looked fine but fragmentation caused many small cudaMallocs during KV cache growth, which pushed kernel selector to choose slower F32 matmul kernels under workspace constraints. perf traces show extra kernel launches and memcpy stalls.

trevor: do you have the profiling snippet? can you paste the critical part?

sam: pasted below. main takeaways:
- batch coalescing decreased throughput (we're dropping from ~85k tokens/s to ~66k tokens/s in the worst case)
- KV cache growth creates transient 10-30MB allocations per request that our arena rounds to 64KB buckets, leading to >20% wasted VRAM in the worst-case mix
- kernel selection prefers "kernel_A_f32" when free workspace < X, but that kernel has ~1.4x latency vs the quantized path

perf-bot: perf snapshot: 1748126790

```
# nvprof-like snippet (abridged)
GPU time breakdown:
matmul_fp32_kernel_A  42.3%
matmul_int8_kernel_Q  29.7%
memcpy_async           12.1%
kernel_launch_overhead 8.9%
other                  7.0%
```

maria: so allocator fragmentation => less workspace => worse kernel chosen => slower overall. we should try: 1) workspace reservation per-model, 2) reuse KV buffers, 3) evict/compact arenas when idle.

lina: +1. Also consider a per-model arena that pre-reserves a small growth slab for KV caches (e.g., reserve_pct of observed 95th percentile). that prevents transient allocations from stalling kernel selection.

trevor: what about swap strategies? when co-resident models exceed VRAM, we could 1) pin cold model weights to host and async-stage when needed, 2) maintain a tiny resident subset (active layers), or 3) do per-request streaming for large embeddings. tradeoffs: latency spikes vs throughput stability.

sam: I prototyped an async-pinned swap that moves whole model weights to pinned host memory and stages on demand. black/white results: average tail latency up ~120ms for cold swaps, but steady-state throughput stable. main pain: cudaMemcpy stalls block kernel selection metrics until copy finishes which confuses the runtime heuristics.

maria: maybe we need a model-residency manager that exposes two numbers to the kernel selector: guaranteed_workspace and optimistic_workspace. the selector then can pick kernels based on guaranteed (safe) and fallback pre-warmed kernel for optimistic path.

lina: sounds good. also allocator tuning: switch from 64KB bucket rounding to a mixed strategy:
- small allocations (< 4KB): fine-grained freelist
- medium (4KB-1MB): power-of-two bins with 4KB increments
- large (>1MB): dedicated mmap-like slabs
This reduces internal fragmentation and keeps arena compaction cheap.

sam: here's a config snippet I sketched for experiments — please try on staging nodes with mixed load (chat + long context reranks):
```yaml
allocator:
  type: pooled
  arena_mb: 32768
  small_bin_kb: 4
  medium_bin_kb: 64
  large_threshold_mb: 1
  enable_compact: true
  compact_idle_s: 30
model_residency:
  policies:
    - name: reserved_percentile
      percentile: 95
      reserve_mode: slab
    - name: async_swap
      strategy: pinned_host
      swap_threshold_pct: 0.9
kernel_selector:
  use_optimistic_workspace: true
  workspace_margin_pct: 0.1
  fallback_kernel: quantized_q8
batching:
  coalesce_window_ms: 6
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  prefer_low_latency: false
```

trevor: nice. couple more quick ideas: 1) implement a background compaction pass that merges free spans when GPU idle (use a low-priority stream), 2) add a KV cache pool with fixed-size chunks to avoid per-request allocs, 3) instrument kernel selector to emit "why-chosen" telemetry so we can track decisions across evictions.

maria: agree. also add an experiment that forces kernel_selector to simulate higher workspace (artificially increase reported free mem) to see if kernel choice alone recovers perf — that'll isolate allocator impact vs true model memory needs.

perf-bot: scheduled perf-run 1748127000 (staging-co-residency-1). will push results here. :rocket:

deploy-bot: rolling a canary with allocator v2 to 3% of capacity (canary id: alloc-v2-2026-03-17). watch logs at /ops/alloc-v2.

lina: action items:
- sam: upload nvprof traces + heap dumps from the run (already saved under /tmp/alloc-traces/1748126789)
- trevor: wire in kernel_selector telemetry (why-chosen) and add test harness to replay decisions against heap snapshots
- maria: implement KV fixed-chunk pool prototype (local branch kv-pool)
- perf-bot: run canary profile and attach flamegraphs

sam: thanks — I'll drop the traces and baseline numbers tonight. once we have "why-chosen" traces we can correlate fragmentation -> kernel decision -> latency. :thinking:

trevor: if compaction + KV pool reduces >10% fragmentation we should see kernel selection shift back to quantized kernels and throughput recovery. fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:

maria: tagging @infra-team later today for discussion about reserved device memory vs dynamic partitioning for co-residency limits. we might want a soft-limiter that prevents new model loads if free < X.

sam: cool — will follow up with results and attach the perf-bot artifacts. thanks everyone.
